test(watchsync): wait for the admission lock until the test deadline

## Problem

Related issue: N/A
Validation tasks: none

`TestSyncRunAdmissionDB` sometimes fails in the Go DB pins job with "repository operation did not enter the expected PostgreSQL lock wait" although nothing is wrong. Its helper looked for the lock wait 128 times in a tight loop and then gave up, and on a busy runner the blocked query can reach the server after those checks run out. This change keeps checking until the test's 30-second deadline.

## Approach

`awaitAdmissionLock` still waits on server state (`pg_blocking_pids` for the blocked connection); it now polls every millisecond until it sees the wait or the test's context ends, instead of stopping after a fixed number of checks.

## Validation

- `TestSyncRunAdmissionDB` against a migrated Postgres 18 database: 5 of 5 runs pass.
- The failure showed up in a full DB pins run where each package had its own fresh database (#3927); it has not recurred in two full runs since this change.

## Evidence

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/pr-3925/

## Risks

A test whose operation never blocks now fails after 30 seconds instead of at once.

Read PyPI release times without building the whole document

With cooldown on, every simple index request and every download reads the package's JSON API document (`/pypi/<name>/json`) for its upload times. `fetchReleaseTimes` decoded it into `map[string]any`, which holds the whole document in memory at several times its size. For botocore (4.4 MB) that was about 17 MB per request, also when everything was cached. An installer resolving many packages at once multiplies it.

The times are now decoded into a struct that names only `releases[].upload_time_iso_8601`, so the rest of the document is skipped. A value of an unexpected type is still ignored as before, not an error.

Parsing a 2.7 MB document (300 releases, 12 files each):

| | time | allocated |
|---|---|---|
| before | 11.3 ms | 12.1 MB |
| after | 4.2 ms | 0.2 MB |

Against pypi.org with `cache_metadata` and a 3 day cooldown, everything cached:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/pypi/simple/botocore/`, allocated per request | 23.5 MB | 6.4 MB |
| 20 simple pages in parallel, allocated | 292 MB | 81 MB |
| 20 simple pages in parallel, peak heap | 264 MB | 87 MB |

What is left is mostly reading the two cached documents.

`TestPyPIParseReleaseTimesAllocatesLessThanDocument` fails without the change. `TestPyPIParseReleaseTimes` passes before and after it.

fix(ui): bound the text of a log by its size

## What changes

A log screen keeps at most 64 MiB of text as well as 50,000 lines. When a followed log goes past either limit, the oldest lines are dropped, as they already were at 50,000 lines. Reading back with `e` stops at the same limit, and the guide in `docs/allocations.md` says so.

None.

fix(ui): clean what the cluster writes before it is drawn

## What changes

The screen reaches the terminal as text, line breaks, colours and styles only. Any other control character or escape sequence in a name, path, spec, error or log line is dropped before the screen is drawn. A line break inside a cell of a table no longer pushes the rows under it down.

## Issues

None.

+// hostile is what a cluster or a task can put in a name, a path, a spec or
+// an error: sequences a terminal acts on, between two letters of text.
+const hostile = "x\x1bP+q544e\x1b\\\x1b_Gf=100;AAAA\x1b\\\x1b]52;c;ZWNobw==\x07\x1b[2J\ry"
+
+var colourCode = regexp.MustCompile(`\x1b\[[0-9;:]*m`)

+// requireOnlyText fails when the screen holds more than text, line breaks
+// and colours.
+func requireOnlyText(t *testing.T, screen string) {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	for _, r := range colourCode.ReplaceAllString(screen, "") {
+		if r != '\n' && unicode.IsControl(r) {
+			t.Fatalf("the screen holds %U:\n%q", r, screen)
+		}
+	}
+}
+

+			return typeCommand(m, "nodepools")

+		{"the path of a file in the title", func(t *testing.T) Model {
+			m, _ := sessionModel(t, &fakeClient{})
+			m, _ = m.update(openMsg{filesPage{namespace: "production", allocID: "abcdef1234", path: "/web/" + hostile}})
+
+			return m
+		}},
+		{"a job spec", func(t *testing.T) Model {
+			m, _ := sessionModel(t, &fakeClient{})
+			m, _ = m.update(describeMsg{label: "Job spec: web", content: "job \"web\" {\n  # " + hostile + "\n}"})
+
+			return m
+		}},
+		{"an error on the status line", func(t *testing.T) Model {
+			m, _ := sessionModel(t, &fakeClient{})

+			return m.fail(errors.New("refused: " + hostile))
+		}},
+	}

+	for _, c := range cases {
+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {

fix(agent): preserve named Center TLS over userspace private transport

Relates to #1214.

No-TUN userspace management previously accepted only a literal tailnet address, preventing enrollment when the Center certificate identifies a hostname. With the existing root-protected transport policy, resolve a named management destination, require every address to belong to the tailnet, and pin that address while retaining the original TLS authority and CA validation. Public destinations keep their ordinary transport.

No dependencies, tests, production control-plane settings, or application configuration are added. Use the existing required CI for the exact head. One-node enrollment and actual service/subscription acceptance remain pending under #1214.

fix(backendauth): keep the GCP ADC token source alive across config reloads

**Description**

The GCP handler builds its ADC token source with the context it is created under (`newGCPHandler` → `google.FindDefaultCredentials(ctx, …)` → `creds.TokenSource`). Handlers are created inside `LoadConfig`, which the bundle watcher runs under a per-tick context that it cancels as soon as the load returns. `external_account` credentials (Workload Identity Federation from EKS/AKS/self-hosted Kubernetes) keep that context for every token exchange, so after the first configuration reload every request to a GCP backend fails with `… Post "https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token": context canceled` until the extproc restarts.

This detaches the token source from the load context with `context.WithoutCancel` and adds a regression test: build the handler, cancel its context, exchange a token against a local `httptest` STS. The test fails on `main` with the production error and passes with the change.

**Related Issues/PRs (if applicable)**

Fixes #2722

**Special notes for reviewers (if applicable)**

- Only ADC of type `external_account` is affected. GKE Workload Identity uses the metadata-server token source, which takes no context; the AWS handler passes the request context to `Retrieve(ctx)`.
- Alternative considered: moving the GCP handler to `cloud.google.com/go/auth` (already in `go.mod`), whose `TokenProvider.Token(ctx)` would let `Do` pass the request context per call. Larger change; happy to follow up with it if you prefer that direction.

fix: accept a whole number a float64 holds exactly as a float64

## Why

`validateFloat64Value` accepted only a Go `float64`. Task outputs, however, are decoded with integers kept exact: `common.NormalizeJSONNumbers` tries `Int64()` first. JSON does not tell `5` from `5.0`, and both JavaScript's `JSON.stringify(5.0)` and RFC 8785 write `5`. So a whole `float64` value reached validation as an `int64` and was refused. A Node task returning `5.0` for a `float64` field failed its own output contract with `$[0].score: expected float64, got int64`.

This is now urgent. Since brokoli-jvm#21, the JVM SDK writes a whole `float64` default as `5`, and the Python and TypeScript SDKs will too once #982 lands. Found by the JVM SDK.

## What changed

**`pkg/taskinterface/value.go`.** A new helper, `float64Of`, reads a `float64` value:
- a `float64` as itself;
- an `int64`, `int` or `json.Number` as the `float64` that holds it exactly, up to 2^53 in magnitude.

Bounds then apply as for the equal `float64`. Beyond 2^53 the value is refused as `a whole number a float64 cannot hold exactly`. This is the mirror of #979, which bounds the other direction.

Values pass through unchanged. Validation decides whether a value is a valid `float64`, so a downstream consumer of a `float64` column can still see a whole number as an integer, as it already could for values decoded elsewhere.

## How it was verified

- **Unit test,** `TestValidateValue_Float64_AcceptsAWholeNumberAFloat64HoldsExactly`. It accepts `int64(5)`, 0, ±2^53, Go `int` 5, `json.Number("5")` and `json.Number("0.25")`. It refuses ±(2^53 + 1) as `int64`, as `int` and as `json.Number`, and still refuses a string. It checks that `minimum`/`maximum` apply to an `int64`.
- **End to end, through the real Node harness:** `TestNodeTaskReturningAWholeFloat64PassesItsOutputContract`, a Node task returning `[{score: 5.0}, {score: 0.5}]` for a `float64` field. On the old check it fails with the exact error from the issue. It passes with the fix.
- **Mutations.** Removing the bound, tightening it to `<`, and letting the `int` path skip the bound each fail a test. The last one survived at first, so I added a Go `int` beyond 2^53 to the refused cases.
- **Suites.** `go test ./pkg/... ./engine/... ./api/... -count=1` passes, 34 packages.

Closes #983
